To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gamma oscillations are robust against changes in the energy metabolism of brain tissue, which may be relevant for the understanding of their role in cognitive functions.
cholinergic-induced gamma oscillations are robust against changes in the nutrient and amino acid content of the cerebro-spinal fluid.

gamma oscillations in the hippocampus are robust against changes in the composition of the extracellular environment, which include the replacement of the main energy substrate glucose by ketone bodies, and that supplementation with glycine increases gamma oscillation frequency and coherence.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the metabolic modulation of fast neuronal oscillations in a model of the hippocampus, a brain structure that is critically involved in the pathophysiology of epilepsy, stroke, and Alzheimer’s disease.
a better understanding of how the brain adapts to metabolic changes in the environment and how this may affect the generation of fast brain rhythms and higher cognitive functions.
the metabolic regulation of neuronal gamma oscillations and their modulation by astrocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

gamma oscillations are highly sensitive to changes in the availability and composition of the energy substrates and that the modulation of their properties can be achieved with different metabolic interventions.
the cholinergic gamma-oscillations are robust against the tested metabolic conditions.
the metabolic modulation of gamma oscillations depends on the experimental conditions and the brain area investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabolic state of neurons and astrocytes can be modulated by the availability of energy substrates, amino acids, and other metabolic factors.
gamma oscillations in vitro are robust to metabolic changes in nutrient and energy supply.
the brain can use different energy substrates and neurotransmitter precursors to maintain the integrity of gamma oscillations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metabolic modulation of gamma oscillations can be used as a tool for studying the mechanisms that underlie the regulation of cortical information processing.
metabolic modulation of neuronal network activity is a promising approach for understanding the role of energy supply in cognitive functions.
gamma oscillations in the brain are robust and can be modulated, for example, by ketone bodies, which may be relevant in the context of metabolic disease, such as diabetes, and ketogenic diet.
